title: ControlMessage
description: Every control message that crosses between a host and the core.

oneOf.description: Starts a run.

contract.description: The contract version the host speaks; see `CONTRACT_VERSION`.

oneOf.description: The host's answer to one fetch.
The host's answer to one model call.
What a run asks of its host next.

Present the pending warnings before requesting the next step.
No data reply is required; cancel or close instead of continuing if the
host's warning policy raises. The core has not crossed the boundary.
Answer every one of these before asking for the next step.
A call to the model; the host sends the body's bytes as they are.

The sampler state a `materialize` run left, which the host takes
once the run has ended, done or failed, and hands back with the
materializer's next `materialize` (decision E52).

A message the core wrote whose encoding would pass the control cap:

Attachments.description:
What each bytes attachment holds that a control message names and the
core reads or writes as JSON, by `<type>.<field>` of the field naming
it: part of the locked schema (`$defs/Attachments`, put there by
[`crate::schema_json`]), so a change to an attachment's shape needs a
version bump as a change to a control message's does. A model call's
body and the endpoint's answer are the endpoint's bytes, and an Arrow
attachment carries its own schema; neither is listed.

AttachmentId.description:
Names an attachment that travels beside a control message: Arrow data
(a fetch's result, a key set, a predict result) or bytes (a model
request or response body).

DecodedDirectRow.description: One actual decoded item with pure key/occurrence facts derived once.

Scalar.description: The encoded form: what crosses the boundary, field for field.

oneOf.description: The unscaled integer: the value is `v * 10^-s`.
Standard base64 with padding.

TimestampUnit.description:
A timestamp's physical count unit. Unlike durations and times of day,
native frame timestamps retain seconds and milliseconds without scaling.

Unit.description: The admitted unit of a duration or time of day.

JsonObservation.description: An actual native JSON conversion of one reached eligible ID.

BuiltinValue.description: Native parsed builtin facts. Nonprimitive members do not acquire display text.

RelationalEncodedCall.description:
One strict native JSON encoding at its actual transport boundary.
The bytes are authoritative, including native Unicode escaping and
members not interpreted by the SDK. No native owner crosses this value.

CallPreparation.description: Each call state has useful resolved facts, never a native action/handle.

NativeCallCapabilities.description: Native capability observations retained independently of the later task read.

ModelEndpoint.description:
The model endpoint a `predict`'s calls go to, as the caller configured
its transport ([`Predict::model_endpoint`]).

oneOf.description:
A Databricks Model Serving endpoint: its name, and the most bytes
one request may take once wrapped in the endpoint's envelope
(`max_request_bytes`, `CL/core/databricks_serving.py:127-148`).

refused.description: Original native sorted-set refusal population, by ordinal.

statistic_option.description: Reached native membership of output_type, only for a refusal.

NativeOutputRole.description: Model-specific preflight questions over actual native data observations.

kind.description: Actual reached native str(task.kind), retaining all codepoints.

mapping.description: The actual native instance-table mapping category at this read.

rows_present.description: Native rows truth, after the mapping guard, without row traversal.

NativeTargetEquality.description:
One original native set observation, not a precomputed semantic count.
Source ordinals refer to rows reached by this particular traversal.
Native object identities used to establish them never cross this boundary.

RelationalTargetPopulation.description: Actual target population, useful independently of warning presentation.

equality.description: Absent when the native context does not expose a target population.

RelationalTargetNaming.description: The core-selected meaning of a constant target's displayed name.

DirectBody.description: Later observations of the same captured frames, before native inference.

TabularColumns.description: Core-resolved schema and wire widths, before text advice and row encoding.

float_storage.description: Native missingness representation, not a casting decision.

ColumnType.description: A type of the closed set.

oneOf.description:
`entries` is the name of Arrow's entries struct, kept so the type
leaves exactly as it came.

Field.description: A named, typed column or child of a nested type.

metadata.description: Arrow field metadata, kept as it came.

IndexType.description: The index type of a dictionary.

RelationalAttribution.description: Native table facts read only after this response was decoded.

source_rows.description: None means the native columns contain no entity reference.

DecodedRelationalRow.description: Generated-decoder values, before native attribution or declared casts.

prior_ordinal.description: Earlier answer to the same (row, step), independent of row validity.

oneOf.description:
Complete postorder container data. Child ordinals are local to this
value's nodes, never attachment handles or instructions. Scalars use
the same exact integer/float/Unicode facts as the ordinary form.

forecasting.description: Actual reached truth of the retained native task comparison.

RelationalInstanceText.description: The actual reached native str(instance), not a sent JSON snapshot.

different.description: Actual reached native str(id) != str(instance) truth.

RelationalResponseData.description: Complete owned decoded response and native-presentation rows.

RelationalResponsePart.description: Independently useful, complete data for layout and later core merging.

RelationalTargetFacts.description:
The actual native kind display and, only for classifications, reached
dtype truth and native startswith(tuple) observations.

classification.description: Actual reached substring comparison, including native overrides.

candidates.description:
Internal JSON carriers; native public values are presented by
candidate position. A native-only carrier is JSON null.

RelationalRowLineage.description: Every laid-out item names its actual call and original native source row.

InterpretedDirectRow.description: Native JSON data with the core's checked representation and catch policy.

SelectedDirectMember.description: A selected member of a checked row, independently useful builtin data.

DirectPrelude.description: Fresh observations at the pre-warning one-shot overlap boundary.

HeldSchema.description:
A schema as a host holds it, as plain data (contract v28, T3.16): its
tables, columns, meanings, keys, time columns and links as they stand,
however the host came to hold them (described, built by hand, edited,
copied or unpickled), and, on each column the source was asked of,
what the source said of it ([`SourceFacts`]). `edit_schema` and
`materialize` read it as it is; `materialize` asks the source for the
facts of a column that carries none, as `describe_source` reads them.

tables.description:
The host's tables as they stand, in its order, each by the name the
schema gives it.

links.description:
The host's relationships as they stand, each
`[foreign key, referenced key]`.

HeldTable.description: One table as the host holds it.

source.description:
The relation of the source it reads, as the host holds it (design
choice 12).

frame_key_form.description: Native frame key representation; absent for ordinary SQL schemas.

duplicate_keys.description:
Rows sharing a key value, as the host holds it
([`DescribedTable::duplicate_keys`]): a `u64` scalar, or none.
`edit_schema` sets it as a key edit does; `materialize` does not
read it. Absent from the JSON when none.

Relation.description:
What a request reads: a relation of the source, by its name's parts,
each quoted alone and never split on a dot, so `["a.b"]` is one table
named `a.b` and `["main", "t"]` the table `t` of `main` (design choice
12). Plain data, a list of strings, as easily built by a host in any
language as a name is. How many parts a source takes is its dialect's:
`sdm-data` renders every dialect's `FROM` from a relation through one
function and refuses one of no part, or of more parts than its dialect
accepts, by name (rule `relation`); a host provider refuses one it
cannot read the same way. Two schema tables over one source are two
equal relations.

A relation may be derived (contract v28, design choice 3 of Phase 3):
`columns`, where given, are the relation's columns, each a name with
the source column it reads or an SQL text expression over the source's
columns, and `filter` an SQL text condition every row read holds, as a
view's definition gives them. Both are text of the source's own SQL,
opaque to the core, which never reads or writes them: only a provider
declaring [`ProviderCapabilities::derived_relations`] is asked for a
derived relation, and the core refuses one for any other by name (rule
[`DERIVED_RULE`]).

columns.description:
The relation's columns, in order, where it is derived; empty, the
source's own columns under their own names; or, where `found`, the
columns the source's catalog found.

filter.description:
The condition, in the source's SQL, every row of the relation holds;
left out, every row of the source is the relation's.

found.description:
The columns are the ones the source's catalog found, each read by
its own name, with no filter (T3.4, round 2): a provider may read
the table through them, so that one since dropped or renamed fails
the read rather than reading anything else by its name (the
reference's Databricks reads, `_quoted_source_name`), or read the
table whole where no column needs it. Left out, `false`: the
columns, if any, are the relation's own.

RelationColumn.description:
One column of a derived relation: the name the relation gives it, and
what it reads, exactly one of a column of the source (`column`) or an
expression in the source's SQL over its columns (`expression`).

HeldColumn.description: One column as the host holds it.

untyped.description: Native inference carried no type, independently of its placeholder dtype.

stype_declared.description: The caller explicitly assigned this meaning, rather than inference.

dtype.description:
The column's data type as the host names it, on the client's wire
([`Dtype::wire_name`]).

stype_before_key.description:
What the column meant before the schema joined on it, as the host
holds it ([`DescribedColumn::stype_before_key`]).

source.description:
What the source said of the column when it was described or last
edited, as the core answered it; absent from the JSON for a column
the source was never asked of (built by hand). A column with none,
or with facts of another relation than its table's, is one whose
facts `materialize` reads from the source, and which `edit_schema`
edits by its data type, as the reference's setters do.

SourceFacts.description:
What the source said of one column ([`DescribedColumn`]'s facts), which
a host keeps on the column and hands back whole (contract v28, T3.16).

relation.description:
The relation of the source the facts were read from: a column of a
table the host points at another relation since holds facts of none
of it, and is read afresh, as one with none is.

dtype.description:
The data type the source's catalog and values give the column
([`DescribedColumn::dtype`]), which tells a date from a time of day
where the wire's name does not.

received.description:
The type the provider handed over, after admission
([`DescribedColumn::received`]).

declared_type.description: [`DescribedColumn::declared_type`]; absent from the JSON when none.

exact_number.description: [`DescribedColumn::exact_number`]; absent from the JSON when none.

ExactNumber.description:
A column of numbers handed over as their exact text
([`DescribedColumn::exact_number`]), by what its catalog declares of it.

oneOf.description:
The catalog declares it a key, the one column of a primary, unique
or foreign key: always read as its text, as the reference reads it.
Any other: its text while the schema keys or joins on it, as above.

FrameKeyForm.description: A native scalar name or ordered key sequence, even of one column.

DirectEnvelope.description: The adapter captures these references after the earlier overlap advice.

DirectOverlap.description: Core-checked prelude and overlap counts, before adapter reference capture.

Given.description:
A value a caller gave an edit or `describe_source`: the value, as the
contract writes it, or a value of the host's own no contract type holds
(a key named by a number, a set of names, a relationship that is not
one), which the core refuses as the reference refuses it.

The conformance rule every host holds to (decision E101): the host's
null or none is `{"value": null}`; text is the value; a finite, ordered
collection read once without error, every member non-null text, is a
list of those texts; a collection with a null, non-text or nested
member, a collection with no order, a mapping, binary data, a number, a
boolean, a temporal value or anything else is `unreadable`. Text the
host cannot encode as UTF-8 is the host's encoding refusal, and an
error raised while reading a collection is the caller's, never
`unreadable`. Whether a value is valid (an empty key, a column the
table lacks) is the core's call, never the host's.

A value no contract type holds may instead be given `{"spelled":
"<text>"}`, the text the host's language shows it as (in Python, its
`repr`): the core takes it as `unreadable` and names it in its refusal
(`given`), as the reference names it, a value of the caller's own call
(KO2-86, T2.14b).

ConstructorContext.description: Settled early constructor guards, before schema inference reads/advice.

ConstructorSchema.description: Settled inferred or supplied meaning, before later native frame observations.

links.description:
The relationships, each `[foreign key, referenced key]`, once: in a
description `describe_source` answers, the declared foreign keys and
the links inferred by name that can join, in that order (decision
E55); in `materialize`'s schema, the host's.

source.description:
The relation of the source this table reads (design choice 12): its
own name, one part, unless the caller named it otherwise (decision
E59).

frame_key_form.description: Native frame key representation; absent for ordinary SQL schemas.

time_column_inferred.description:
The column inference took as the time column, when the table's
time column is now another or none: a lone stamp of the last edit a
link then refused (decision E55), or the column inference took where
the caller named another (decision E59). `None` when the time column
is inference's, or inference took none. The host's schema was
ordered by it first, as the reference's was; `materialize` does not
read it.

duplicate_keys.description: Rows sharing a key value, when keys were checked: a `u64` scalar.

untyped.description: Native inference carried no type, independently of its placeholder.

received.description: The type the provider handed over, after admission.

stype.description:
What the column means in the schema as it stands: `ID` for a column
the schema joins on, its primary key or a link's foreign key
(decision E55).

stype_before_key.description:
What the column meant before the schema's joining on it made it an
identifier, given back when the schema stops joining on it; `None`
when joining on it changed nothing, or it is not joined on. In a
description `describe_source` answers, the core's; in `materialize`'s
schema, what the host holds, from which the core marks the columns
joined on again (decision E55).

nullable.description:
Whether the column may hold no value, as the catalog declares it:
neither declared `NOT NULL` nor part of the declared primary key.

unique.description:
Whether the catalog declares a primary or unique key of this one
column, which the source refuses to repeat.

declared_type.description:
The source's opaque catalog declaration, retained for numeric and
temporal columns and marked big integers.
A dialect uses it to preserve exact numeric key joins and destination
float coercion, and to distinguish zoned instants from NTZ wall clocks.
Other columns keep none. Absent when none.

exact_number.description:
Set for a column of numbers the host provider handed over as their
exact decimal text (marked [`crate::data::EXACT_NUMBER_MARKER`]):
whether its catalog declares it a key. The schema reads such a column
by its role in the schema as it stands (T2.21): as its text
(`received` `utf8`, `dtype` `string`) where the catalog declares it a
key, or where the schema keys it or joins it and every column it
joins to is such a column too; as a double (`float64`) otherwise.
`None` for every other column, and absent from the JSON.

ConstructorTaskTable.description: Only the selected native table's names and selected target's dtype.

PreparedValue.description: The closed data value answered by one fixed preparation stage.

RelationalCallFields.description:
Concrete fields selected by shared request policy. Native values and
shallow container copies remain in the host until the transport encodes.

PreparedDirectTask.description: Model-neutral task metadata, resolved after constructor advice effects.

EncodedDirectBody.description:
A complete valid tabular envelope before optional metadata/inference.
It is independently inspectable wire data, without deferred commands.

CheckedDirectRows.description: Consecutive pure rows plus at most one reached native representation.

CheckedRelationalRows.description: A checked prefix and, if present, the first reached native forecast truth.

lineage.description: Final answer_index order, retaining each original response ordinal.

Predicted.description:
The prediction. Nothing inline grows with the result's width or the
endpoint's answer (decision H5).

result.description:
An Arrow attachment, one row per answer, ordered by `row_index` as
the reference's result frame orders them (T1.28b), whose schema
names its columns in order: `row_index`, `id`, `id_as_written` where
the ids are not all integers or all text (utf8: the JSON text of the
reference's item value, null where there was none), `forecast_step`
where an answer given as written carries one, `prediction` where an
answer carries one, `prediction_as_answered` where the prediction
column changed an answer (utf8: the JSON text of the reference's item
value, null where there was none; present only for a regression's
integer widened among doubles or a class written as a non-finite
number), `probabilities` where an answer carries them, and
`answer_index`, each answer's place in the endpoint's order
(`sdm_request::predict::table`).

Contract v26 fixes the columns ranking and forecasting add (design
choice 1; written from T2.8 and T2.9), after `probabilities` and
before `answer_index`, each where an answer carries it: `scores`
(list of float64, an item's scores in the endpoint's order),
`rankings` (list of utf8, an item's rankings, each a mapping), and
`quantiles` (a regression's quantiles, each named as the endpoint
named it, in the order written; from contract v27, T2.9, a
mapping-valued field, laid out as the next paragraph says, an
answer's `{}` the text `{}`, none null).

A mapping-valued field (T2.8, contract v27) is laid out as JSON
object text in a Utf8 column, and a list of mappings as a list of
those texts: a JSON object when every key is text, otherwise (a key
that is a number, a boolean or null) the JSON list of its `[key,
value]` pairs, as a JSON object holds no other key. Each is read
from the answer as Python's `dict` reads it, keys equal as Python's
are, by the one reader `sdm_wire::response::mapping`.

A ranking's result (T2.8, contract v27), one row per entity asked
about, in place
of `prediction` and `probabilities`: `rankings` (the candidates the
row ranks, best first, at most `top_k`, each the JSON text of its
value, as the state names it), `scores` (how sure the endpoint was
of each, in the same order) and `candidates` (list of int64, each
one's position among the candidates `materialize` was given, its
first where it was given more than once, in the same order), which a
host gives back as the outputs named in `outputs`, each candidate as
the value it was given as, found by its position.

Contract v27 adds, after those, `embeddings` (list of float64, an
answer's embedding in the order written, null where it has none;
T2.11).

model.description: The model that answered, as the endpoint names it.

request_id.description:
The endpoint's id for the call; empty for a request with no row to
score, answered without a call.

metadata.description: A bytes attachment of the endpoint's `metadata` object as JSON.

outputs.description:
The outputs the call asked for, the task's default ones where the
caller named none.

unscored_candidates.description:
A ranking's candidates no question was sent for, the context sampled
for each holding one answer only (T2.8): each its position among the
candidates `materialize` was given (of a request held, among the
candidates it holds, T3.26), in the order named. Empty for any other
result.

Sentence.description:
What an error or a warning says: one variant per distinct
sentence, each with the one template every host fills
([`crate::wording::template`]). The core picks it; a host only
fills it.

Detail.description: A value under an error's or a warning's `fields`.

DirectPredict.description:
Source-position body observations after core-selected text advice.
Later values/kind may legitimately differ from the checked prelude.

DirectInference.description:
Ordered flat primitive inference values; exact integer digits do not
acquire serde_json's machine-integer limit before final wire policy.

FrameInference.description: Fixed data products of shared native-frame constructor boundaries.

FrameNomination.description: Independently inspectable inference facts, before native adoption reads.

missing.description: Actual inferred-key isna.any result, before its possible warning.

FrameAdoption.description: Key metadata/count fixed before a possible repeat warning is presented.

FrameTimePlan.description: Core-selected native first-value reads in original candidate order.

FrameTimeFirst.description: Values/counts read by actual native dropna/iloc/equality operations.

FrameScalar.description:
A completed native scalar conversion, not an instruction to the host.
Decimal tuples retain actual native boxing, including a full exponent,
separately from both constructor mantissas and later model wire values.

oneOf.description:
The native source has not reached a conversion of this scalar.
It is neither an object handle nor a claim that the value is absent.

FrameInferred.description: Completed table inference, including the later time observations.

TimeChoice.description:
The time column inference took and how, and the timestamps it passed
over, as the reference's `TimeColumnChoice` holds them.

instead_of.description: The view dimensions that truncate or cast the chosen raw column.

among.description: The columns it was chosen from, itself included.

refused.description:
Every timestamp passed over, in table order, the lone edit stamp
taken as the last resort included.

fallback.description: The lone edit stamp left, when no other timestamp was.

unconfirmed.description:
Where the whole table was asked about and its answer failed, each
timestamp the preview's rows would pass over for its values, kept
(behind every column they do not) and named, its counts the rows
read (`TimeColumnChoice.unconfirmed`).

Taken.description:
How the time column was taken (`TimeColumnChoice.how`): the one
timestamp left, the one creation stamp among several, the one whose
values start earliest, or a lone stamp of the last edit in a table no
other links to.

PassedOver.description:
Why inference passed a timestamp over for the time column, as the
reference's `RejectedTimeColumn` holds it: its values (no row holds
one, or every row that holds one holds the same; more than half the
rows hold none), or its name (a stamp of a row's load, of its last edit,
or a date of birth).

oneOf.description:
No row holds a value (`value` `None`), or the table has more than
one row and every row that holds one holds `value`; `missing` of
its `rows` rows hold none.

A native frame's completed first-value read, kept independently of
physical Arrow storage and its narrower Decimal scalar descriptor.
`missing` of its `rows` rows, more than half, hold no value.

FrameSchema.description:
Complete assembled meaning and independently usable sample-column plans.
Metadata-only advice is retained until its native source position.

FrameSampleColumn.description: The fixed original meaning of one column whose cardinality decided it.

CoreWarning.description: A warning a run gives, kept in the order given.

code.description: The sentence's [`WarningCode`], as the contract spells it.

FrameKeyAdvicePlan.description: Final declared schema populations before native keyless advice reads.

FrameSample.description: Current native cardinality facts at one actual column-read position.

FrameManifest.description: The ordered Arrow tables admitted for one describe call.

inference.description: Prior useful table facts, carried separately from fresh Arrow rows.

override_order.description:
Native mapping order, separate from SourceSpec's value maps.
Empty/default only when both maps are empty.

key_forms.description: Native scalar/sequence form of each explicit key override.

relationships.description: The single authoritative ordered explicit link list, or inference.

FrameStage.description: Fixed constructor stages, never configurable inference policies.

FrameInput.description: A stable literal source name bound to this message's Arrow data.

decimals.description: Original native Decimal types of this attachment's typed mantissas.

objects.description: Native object/category cells and their reached column meanings.

NativeDecimalColumn.description: One logical native Decimal type bound to the same FrameInput field.

NativeDecimal.description:
Original logical type beside admitted scale-zero Decimal mantissa storage.
Native scale is the complete signed-i32 fact, including scale greater
than precision; it is not narrowed to Arrow Rust's physical i8 scale.

NativeObjectColumn.description:
One native scalar column, bound by both physical ordinal and source name.
An unconverted scalar is a category/presence observation, never a handle.

NativeObjectMeaning.description: The result of the core-selected native object inference traversal.

distinct.description: Actual native nunique at the reached string-meaning boundary.

FrameRelationship.description: One native relationship argument at its original validation position.

oneOf.description: Native presentation facts only; the core decides this slot is invalid.

MaterializeFrames.description:
The first frame materializer's ordered, call-local Arrow bindings.
Unlike constructor stages, this manifest names no inference policy.

tables.description: Empty only when a frame checkpoint supplies the frozen snapshot.

entropy.description:
Fresh OS entropy supplied by the host, consumed only by an unseeded
entity/example sample. Neighbor continuation never reads this fact.

FrameRowIdentity.description: Complete aligned native identity values in original source row order.

FrameCompositeDefinition.description: A complete ordered compound identity, not a conversion cursor or callback.

FrameIdentityComponent.description: Fixed component type, projected independently of overwritten initial stype.

StringEncoding.description:
Closed value encodings, independently of native storage or casing.
Both Arrow offset widths retain their original physical buffers.

oneOf.description: Arrow Utf8 or LargeUtf8, whose values are ordinary Unicode scalars.

Arrow Binary or LargeBinary, containing canonical UTF8 with
surrogatepass. Adjacent surrogate points remain distinct points.

FrameCheckpointManifest.description:
Ownership bindings of a materializer's detached frame snapshot.
The metadata is JSON; every table remains a separately owned Arrow attachment.

retained.description:
The same live core-created graph owner, without exporting source rows.
Raw legacy checkpoints have no retained alternative.

FrameCheckpointMetadata.description:
Core-owned snapshot semantics, opaque to a host retaining the checkpoint.
Arrow data and derived CSC structures never travel inside this JSON.

source.description: Fingerprint of logical schema/source and detached row values, never ids.

Mt19937State.description:
The exact continuing state of the legacy MT19937 primitive.
The consumer validates the 624 words and the position before reading it.

FramePreparation.description:
Fixed operations over useful values, never host instructions or a program.
Each invocation ends normally through the existing Done boundary.

schema.description:
Live logical declarations after physical table admission and before
GraphStore-style native sanitization.

typed_tables.description: Cast-time dtype facts from those same ordered physical tables.

retained.description: A live typed owner avoids replaying raw checkpoint source data.

values.description: Existing early client call-value observations, before graph notices.

question.description: The same original resolved query, before native metadata effects.

entropy.description:
Actual fresh OS fact for an unseeded draw, independent of the
immutable graph checkpoint and its continuing neighbor stream.

previous.description: The last actual evaluated batch and its immutable accepted-prefix facts.

prediction.description: Actual reached native Series constructor result or failure.

values.description: Fresh late request-option facts, observed after HOPS presentation.

converted.description: Actual complete-task native astype(str) outcome, preserving missingness.
Actual later per-batch native cast outcome, before reset and draws.

text.description: Actual reached raw conversions, not just global dtype metadata.

values.description: Native request flags at their reached construction position.

parts.description:
Complete independently encoded calls. No earlier payload is
passed through a later native conversion or payload operation.

FrameTableMeaning.description:
Cast-time table dtype facts and their ordered physical column identities.
Later source composition takes logical metadata from live declarations.

FrameConstructedColumn.description: A core-derived constructed dtype, independent of later caller declarations.

empty.description: Actual reached native container empty observation, before dtype reads.

FrameTableColumnFacts.description:
Physical native source types read during table construction, after all
tables have completed their native declared casts.

FramePhysicalDeclaration.description:
Original reconstruction declaration, independently of exported buffers.
Native Decimal widths and full i32 scale are not narrowed to interchange
admission's widened scale-zero physical representation.

oneOf.description:
Canonical non-Decimal scalar declaration. The shared reader rejects
Decimal interchange variants in favor of the original descriptor below.

FrameConstructorValues.description: Neutral storage/content observed when the physical table is constructed.

oneOf.description: Native Unicode points; the later owned column states its encoding.

FrameKeyNulls.description: The reached missingness observation of one declared component.

FrameTableMetadata.description: The reached same-table declarations after its selected key was assigned.

derived.description: Actual completed new derived column; absent for a pre-existing column.

FrameColumnFacts.description: Actual native storage and inference observations, without schema policy.

FrameObservedContent.description:
The observed scalar content, adapted after one reached native inference.
None at the containing field means inference was not performed.

FrameIntegerColumn.description:
Complete native fractional-mask observations before the whole-value map.
Repr is observed only for the first actual fractional element.

FrameColumnKind.description:
The resolved logical type of one source column. These meanings select
no native callback and carry no execution position.

GivenCandidate.description:
One candidate of a ranking as a host gives it (`Materialize.candidates`,
T2.8), each in one of these forms:

- `{"value": <scalar>}`: the host's value as the contract's scalar of
  its own type, a missing value `null`.
- `{"integer": "<digits>"}`: an integer wider than an integer scalar
  holds, by its digits (`-` before a negative one).
- `{"decimal": "<digits>"}`: an exact decimal of any precision, by its
  fixed-point digits (`-12.50`), its scale the digits after the point.
- `{"spelled": "<text>"}`: a value of a type no scalar holds, by the
  text the reference writes into its question (in Python, `str` of it);
  it is no text candidate, and the core holds it equal to no other.
- `{"typed": {"text": "<text>", "type": "<name>"}}`: a value of a type
  no scalar holds, written into its question by its text as `spelled`
  is, with the name of the kind of value it is (`date`, `datetime` for a
  timestamp with no zone, `datetime_zoned` for one with one, `time`).
  Two of one kind and one text are one candidate; a host whose language
  holds others equal (two zones of one instant) says so with `repeat`
  (T2.14b).
- `repeat`: a value the host's own language holds equal to one given
  before it, left out as the reference's `dict.fromkeys` leaves it out.
  A host whose candidates are all scalars sends none, the core keeping
  each distinct value once by its own equality.
- `unreadable`: a value the host cannot look up by value (in Python,
  one it cannot hash), which names no row and which the core refuses by
  name, as the reference fails on it.
