(KO2-86, T2.14b).

SamplerMemo.description: [`SamplerState`]'s memo: what the runs read, and of what.

source.description:
A fingerprint of the provider and source description the memo was
made under; a memo of another is not read.

indexes_checked.description:
Whether the sampler's check of the indexes its reads would use was
made (and its warning given, if any).

bounds.description: The time bounds read, at most one entry per table.

stored_times.description:
One stored value of each windowed table's time column, read once
where the provider compares a window's bounds with its stored text
(SQLite's `_time_spelling`), at most one entry per table; left out
where none was read.

rows.description:
Each table's rows, read once where the provider's sampling is sized
by them ([`crate::data::ProviderCapabilities::sample_rows`],
`neighbor_lookback`; contract v28), as the reference's warehouse
samplers count every table's rows as they are built; left out where
none was read.

MemoBounds.description:
The smallest and largest time of one table's time column, as read, in
nanoseconds since the epoch; none where no row holds a time.

table.description: The table, as the schema names it.

MemoStoredTime.description:
One table's stored time value, as read: the text of one non-null value
of its time column, or none where that value was not text.

table.description: The table, as the schema names it.
The table, as the schema names it.

HostFacts.description: The facts a host passes with every operation.

now.description: The clock: a `ts` scalar in UTC. Two-digit years and "now" read it.

local_zone.description: The host's local zone, if it knows one.

zone_roots.description:
The zone lookup roots, in the order the host's own zone library
searches them; the core falls back to its bundled database.

date_literal_range.description:
The instants the host can hold a PQL date literal as, when it holds
fewer than the core reads (years 0 to 9999); none when it holds them
all. A literal outside them is refused as one that cannot be read
(`PQL_VALUE_INVALID_LITERAL`), as the reference refuses it on such a
host: pandas 2 holds a literal as a nanosecond `Timestamp`.

A bridge fact: it is needed only because the Python host's S0
shadow check runs the old pandas validator on every query the core
accepts. It is deleted with that check in Phase 5, and the core then
reads years 0 to 9999 on every host.

LocalZone.description:
The host's local zone, as the host's own platform names it: an IANA
name, or a POSIX `TZ` string where the platform has no IANA name for it.

oneOf.description: An IANA zone name, such as `Europe/Berlin`.
A POSIX `TZ` string, such as `EST5EDT,M3.2.0,M11.1.0`.

ZoneRootFact.description: One zone lookup root, with the database version the host read there.

PlatformFacts.description: Platform behavior the reference depends on.

os.description:
The operating system, as the host names it (`linux`, `darwin`,
`windows`).

strftime_pads_year.description:
Whether the platform's `strftime` pads years below 1000 to four
digits (`date-rules.md`).

InstantRange.description:
Instants, inclusive at both ends, as nanoseconds from the Unix epoch on
a literal's own wall clock.

oneOf.description: Validate a predictive query against a schema, for a profile.

query.description: The query text: a bytes attachment of a JSON string.

schema.description: A bytes attachment of a [`QuerySchema`] as JSON.

oneOf.description: Describe the tables of a source: types, keys and time columns.

source.description: A bytes attachment of a [`SourceSpec`] as JSON.

oneOf.description:
Check one edit to a schema and make it, as the reference client's
setters check and make it (decision E67): the schema the host holds, as
plain data, and the edit; the result is the schema with the edit made,
or the refusal the reference gives at the assignment (contract v28,
T3.16: the schema alone, with what the source said of each column on
the column, never a description the core answered earlier).

schema.description:
A bytes attachment of a [`HeldSchema`] as JSON: the host's schema as
it stands.

edit.description: A bytes attachment of a [`SchemaEdit`] as JSON.

oneOf.description: Build a request for a query over a described source.

schema.description:
A bytes attachment of a [`HeldSchema`] as JSON: the schema to
sample, as the host holds it (contract v28, T3.16).

query.description: The query text: a bytes attachment of a JSON string.

indices.description: The entities to predict for: an Arrow attachment of one column.

candidates.description:
The rows a ranking (`RANK TOP k`) is over, as the caller named them
(contract v27, optional, T2.8): a bytes attachment of a JSON list of
[`GivenCandidate`]s, each candidate as the host's value is written,
so values of several types keep each its own. The core asks a
ranking as one question per distinct candidate, writing each into
its question by the type of the column ranked, and refuses
candidates on any other question.

seed.description: The sampling seed, an integer of any size.

unseeded.description:
Whether the caller asked for an unseeded sample, a new one each
call (`random_seed=None`), with `seed` left out; from contract v27
the core draws it under a seed of its own, new each call (T2.11).

anchor_entity.description:
Whether the caller anchored each entity at its own time
(`anchor_time='entity'`), with `anchor_time` left out; from contract
v27 taken for a static query (T2.11).

values.description:
A bytes attachment of a JSON object of the call's option values the
core reads (T1.28a), each as the caller gave it and the host's JSON
writes it, a member only where the call names the option:
`num_context_samples`, the context size, whose run mode the core
chooses and bounds; `num_hops` and `num_neighbors`, whose hops it
bounds before it refuses them by name; `prediction_statistic`, which
it checks and records; `inference_config`, which it reads by the
engine's rules and writes into the payload (decision E45(a)); and
`random_seed`, in place of `seed` and `unseeded` where it is given
(`null`, an unseeded sample); from contract v26, `rows_per_call`,
the most rows one model call scores, which only lowers the profile's
(`main`'s multi-call `predict`, read from T2.8c); `top_k`, how
many candidates a ranking keeps, in place of the query's `TOP k`,
read from T2.8; from contract v27, `lag_timesteps`, the past steps
of a temporal target added as features (T2.9), any value, which the
core refuses where the reference's engine refuses it, once the
context is labelled; and from contract v27 the sampling options
(T2.11): `num_hops` and `num_neighbors`, the hops walked and each
one's size; `max_pq_iterations`; `use_prediction_time`;
`return_embeddings`, which names `embeddings` among the payload's
outputs; `exclude_cols_dict`, as given; and `context_anchor_time`,
written as `anchor_time` is (a `ts` scalar), or as the text
`entity`, `null`, or the text `unreadable` for any other value. The core reads it with `sdm-wire`'s
bounded reader and holds each value's type to what the reference's
client takes, so the host checks none of them.
Working v30's option encoding also preserves bare `NaN`, `Infinity`
and `-Infinity` numeric tokens in this attachment only. The core
admits only a NaN `lag_timesteps` under KO3-44; other nonfinite
option values remain named refusals. Text tokens and ordinary
message JSON retain their existing strict interpretation.

options.description:
The names of the call's other sampling options, which this message
carries no value of (none from contract v27: every sampling option
travels in `values`): the core refuses any name it is given as
`INVALID_REQUEST` (decision E61). The host
passes each the call gave, so it refuses none of its own.

most_parts.description:
The most steps a forecast is asked as, one call each, which the host
lets its caller set (the client's `decompose.MOST_PARTS`); 200 where
it names none. A forecast of more is refused, `INVALID_REQUEST`, rule
`too_many_parts` (T1.36 fix 21).

most_entities.description:
The most entities one `materialize` gathers, across the calls it is
asked in, which the host lets its caller set (`main`'s
`MOST_ENTITIES`); 100,000 where it names none (design choice 1,
multi-call `predict`, read from T2.8c, which asks a request of more
rows than one call scores in several calls; until then the core
refuses more than one call's rows, a lower bound than either).

most_calls.description:
The most model calls one request is asked in (`main`'s
`MOST_CALLS`); 100 where the host names none (read from T2.8c, as
`most_entities`).

sampler_state.description:
The sampler state the materializer's last run left, which the host
hands back as it took it (decision E52); none for a materializer's
first run.

oneOf.description: Send a materialized request to the model and lay out its answer.

direct.description: Closed model-neutral direct-frame input, separate from gathered state.

state.description:
The request state `materialize` answered, as the host held it since;
absent where the host holds a request the core did not
materialize, which [`Predict::held`] gives instead. A start naming
both, or neither, is refused.

held.description:
A request the core did not materialize, as the host holds it (T3.26,
owner decision 2026-10-23): one an older client gathered, or this
one on its old route. The core rebuilds what it predicts from from
it alone, as the old client predicts what such a request holds.

model.description: The model id the request is sent to, as the wire names it.

request_id.description:
The id the request carries in its `metadata.request_id`. The host
draws it, as the reference's client draws one for every request; the
core draws nothing at random but under a seed.

outputs.description:
The outputs the caller asked for, by the wire's names, in order,
as given (a name repeated, kept), which the core checks against the
model as the client's `_prepare` does: an empty list refused
(`INVALID_REQUEST`), a name the model does not produce refused
(`UNSUPPORTED_REQUEST`). Empty when [`Predict::default_outputs`]
for gathered inputs; direct inputs repeat their bound resolved outputs.

default_outputs.description:
The caller named no outputs: the core asks the task's default ones
(a regression's `prediction`, a classification's `prediction` and
`probabilities`), and gives no notice of one the answer leaves out,
which it gives only for outputs the caller named (T1.28b).

inference_asked.description:
The inference-config keys the caller set at `materialize`, rather
than left to their defaults, as the host holds them: a key the model
does not read among them is refused before the call is made, the
others' defaults left out of it silently (T1.28a).

model_endpoint.description:
The model endpoint the host's transport calls, where the core writes
its envelope and reads its answers (contract v28, T3.27, for T3.13):
a Databricks Model Serving endpoint, by name, with the request size
the caller allows it. Left out, the client's own endpoint, as
before.

input.description: FramePreparation as input-sized JSON with explicitly declared owners.

ProfileSpec.description:
A named profile, optionally naming the model in diagnostics and
changing named capabilities, as the language's `Profile.named` and
`Capabilities.also` do. The profiles themselves are the core's.

ProviderChoice.description:
The composition root's choice: a built-in SQL provider by dialect, which
compiles each request to SQL the host runs, or a host provider that
answers the typed requests itself.

A SQL provider's `namespace` (contract v28) is where the source's tables
are, as the source was given it: the name parts before a table's own,
outermost first, a Postgres source's schema (`PostgresSource(schema=...)`),
each `null` where the source names none, which is then the connection's
current one. Every relation of one part a request names is read under
it, and the source's tables are listed in it, as the reference
qualifies each read by the schema it was given (`PostgresTable`). Left
out, empty or all `null`, the connection's current one, as before v28.
A dialect takes as many parts as a relation's parts before its table's,
and refuses by name more, or a part given inside one left `null`.

A SQL provider's `view` (contract v28, T3.27) names the semantic model
the source is read through, a Databricks metric view or a Snowflake
semantic view by its dialect, as the caller named it, with whether the
caller trusts its expressions: its logical tables are then the
relations of one part a request names, each the logical table's name.
Left out, the source's own tables, as before.

oneOf.description:
Frames already admitted for this describe call. This is an internal
core source, never a host provider or a SQL dialect.

timestamp_encoding.description:
A host's required lossless transport for timestamps that its
driver cannot preserve through native getters. The data layer
owns the SQL projection; the host performs only the conversion
explicitly named by the resulting plan.

Dialect.description:
A built-in SQL dialect, by the name the host gives it. The contract
names no dialect and knows none (decision E54): which names a build
serves is the data layer's, which refuses one it does not serve before
the run exists ([`DataLayer::capabilities`]).

ViewChoice.description:
The semantic model a SQL provider's source is read through
([`ProviderChoice::Sql`]'s `view`): its name as the caller gave it, and
whether the caller trusts whoever authored it to run its expressions
(`semantic_model(name, trust_expressions=...)`).

SqlTimestampEncoding.description: A driver's requested lossless SQL timestamp transport.

oneOf.description:
Timestamps as signed microseconds: timezone-free wall fields from
the epoch's wall fields, or a zoned timestamp's physical instant
from the Unix epoch. The core selects the source kind from actual
warehouse result metadata, independent of the session or JVM zone.

ProviderCapabilities.description:
What a provider answers: a host provider declares it, and the data
layer gives it for each SQL dialect it renders.

max_keys_per_request.description: The most keys one request may carry; `None` is no limit.

max_seed.description:
The largest seed the provider samples with (register entry RS-7),
which every provider declares: there is no "any seed" default
(design choice 1). The core refuses a sample with a larger seed,
`INVALID_REQUEST` naming the seed, before the sample is planned;
which seeds a provider takes is the provider's to declare, never a
name the core matches.

null_order.description:
Where the source puts a null when it orders (`NullOrder`); `None`
declares none, and the core refuses to ask it for rows in an order
(`UNSUPPORTED_REQUEST`, rule `null_order`).

index_advice.description:
Which indexes serve the sampler's reads (`IndexAdvice`); `None`
declares no meaningful index advice: the core neither reads the
source's indexes nor warns of missing ones.

fallback.description:
The limits within which the core answers an optional request the
provider does not declare itself, in memory, from the rows a `scan`
reads (design choice 1, the in-memory fallback, T2.6); left out,
the provider declares none, and such a request is refused,
`UNSUPPORTED_REQUEST`, as before. A declared request that fails is
the provider's error either way, never answered by the fallback.

derived_relations.description:
The provider reads derived relations ([`Relation::columns`],
[`Relation::filter`]; contract v28). Left out, `false`: the core
refuses a derived relation for the provider by name (rule
[`DERIVED_RULE`]).

sample_rows.description:
The provider sizes an entity sample by the table's rows, as the
reference's warehouse samplers do (a sampled percentage of the
rows): the core counts each sampled table's rows first and names
the count on the sample ([`DataRequest::SampleEntities`]'s `rows`;
contract v28). Left out, `false`.

neighbor_lookback.description:
The provider's neighbor reads by a foreign key over a table with a
time column look back no further than the reference's warehouse
samplers do (`_by_fkey`): from each seed's anchor back by five
times the rows asked over the table's rate of rows per referenced
row and second, at most five years, the seconds rounded up. The
core counts the table's and the referenced table's rows, reads the
table's time bounds, and bounds each such read from below by that
look-back, exclusive (contract v28). Left out, `false`: no lower
bound.

keys_optional.description:
The provider's catalog may fail to read a table's declared keys and
foreign keys where it reads its columns (Unity Catalog's
`table_constraints` on an older runtime or without the privilege):
the core then reads a table's columns and its keys apart, and reads
a failed key or foreign-key read as no declared keys, as the
reference's Databricks reader carries on without them
(`DatabricksTable`'s key reads; contract v28). Left out, `false`: a
failed key read fails the description.

key_enforcement.description:
The catalog can answer `key_enforcement` for a table's namespace.
This optional fact can skip counting an enforced declared primary
key; it never certifies uniqueness of values exposed by a lookup.

opaque_vendor.description:
The vendor whose opaque Arrow extension types (`arrow.opaque`, its
metadata's `vendor_name`) the provider hands over: the host layer
reads an opaque column by that vendor's layout only when the column
names this vendor (register P1B-43). Left out, none, and no opaque
column is read as anything but its storage (contract v28, carried
row P2-MID2-2: before it, a flag of the data layer's).

compares_stored_times.description:
The provider compares a window's bounds with the stored text of the
window's column, as a source with no time type does (SQLite's
reference spells each bound as one stored value is spelled,
`_time_spelling`): the core then reads one non-null value of a
table's time column (a `scan` of one row) before that table's first
windowed read in a run, and names it on each bound's seed column
([`SEED_STORED_TIME`]). Left out, `false` (P2-MID2-2).

samples_by_key_dtype.description:
The provider orders a seeded sample by the key's data type, as
SQLite's does (it hashes an integer key and the `rowid` otherwise):
the core then names the schema's type of a key of one column on each
`sample_entities` (`key_dtype`). Left out, `false` (P2-MID2-2).

reads_nan_as_missing.description:
The reference reads the provider's rows into a frame of NumPy-backed
floats, where a NaN is missing and `-0.0` is `0.0` (Postgres's rows,
read as Python objects); otherwise as Arrow-backed pandas does, where
a NaN is a value and the two zeros are two values (T2.12). Left out,
`false` (P2-MID2-2).

OptionalRequest.description: The optional requests a provider may declare.

Determinism.description: Whether a provider's seeded sampling repeats.

oneOf.description: The same seed gives the same rows on this provider.

TextTimes.description:
How a provider's source reads a time it stores as text: which of the
reference's two readings the core applies to the text it fetches from
the provider (register DT-7). The provider declares it; the core picks
its reader by it, never by a dialect.

oneOf.description:
Each value on its own, as the reference's engine reads a SQL
source's text time column (`to_datetime(values, unit='ns')`).

The column by the client's rules (`date-rules.md`, "The client
rules"), as the reference reads a frame's time column.

NullOrder.description:
Where a provider's source puts a null among the values it orders, in
either direction: the order the reference's neighbor reads get from the
source, which writes no null order of its own (`_neighbor_order_by`).
The provider declares it; the core writes it into the tie-break it asks
for ([`TieTerm::nulls_last`]), never by a dialect. A source whose order
depends on the direction is not declarable yet: the dialect that needs
one adds it under a new contract version.

oneOf.description: Nulls first, ascending or descending.
Nulls last, ascending or descending.

IndexAdvice.description:
Which of the source's indexes the reference's sampler counts as serving
a read on a key or foreign key, for its warning of the indexes it would
use and finds missing. The provider declares it; the core reads the
source's indexes, and warns, only when it is declared.

oneOf.description:
An index over exactly that one column, its coverage resolved; one
over several columns, or one the reader cannot resolve, serves none.

The reference's SQLite sampler's: each table's indexes read one
table at a time, each index's columns by its name; a read wants an
index on the key, and on each foreign key with its table's time
column, and any index whose first column is the read's first serves
it.

FallbackLimits.description:
The in-memory fallback's limits, as a provider declares them
([`ProviderCapabilities::fallback`]): past either, the fallback fails
by name rather than read on.

max_rows.description: The most rows the fallback reads to answer one request.

max_bytes.description: The most bytes of Arrow data it holds to answer one request.

SamplerState.description:
What a materializer's runs have read of its source, so a later run
skips a read the reference's sampler makes once (decision E52): the
core holds no state across runs. A `materialize` run leaves it, done or
failed, and the host takes it after the run ends (a `sampler_state`
message), keeps it on its materializer as it is, opaque, and hands it
back with that materializer's next `materialize`.

version.description: The version of this state's format, independent of the contract's.

memo.description: A bytes attachment of a [`SamplerMemo`] as JSON.

frame_checkpoint.description:
The numeric frame materializer's owned snapshot and continuing stream.
Absent for SQL samplers; metadata and Arrow have distinct ownership.

HeldRequest.description:
A request the core did not materialize, as the host holds it
([`Predict::held`], T3.26): its public contents only, each payload as the
request holds it and each question's text, with what the host was given
of a ranking's candidates. The core rebuilds from it what a
[`RequestState`] gives: a forecast's later steps numbered from 2, in
order; a ranking's questions named by their place among the candidates
held, each by the JSON text of its value, written from the candidate as
`materialize` writes it; the later calls of a request asked in several,
each scoring the rows after the last. No version applies: nothing in it
was written by a core.

payload.description:
A bytes attachment of the first call's payload as JSON, as the
request holds it: the request's own, a forecast's first step's, or a
ranking's first question's.

query.description:
The first call's question's text: a bytes attachment of a JSON
string.

batches.description:
The later calls of a request asked in several, in order, as
[`RequestState::batches`]. Absent for a request of one call.

forecast.description:
A forecast's later steps, in order, as [`RequestState::forecast`].
Absent for any other request.

ranking.description:
A ranking's candidates and later questions, as
[`RequestState::ranking`]. Absent for any other request.

HeldCall.description: A later call of a request held asked in several ([`HeldRequest::batches`]).

payload.description: A bytes attachment of this call's payload as JSON.

request_id.description:
The id this call carries, which the host draws for each call, as
[`RequestBatch::request_id`].

HeldPart.description:
A later part of a request held asked in parts: a forecast's step or a
ranking's question, in order.

payload.description: A bytes attachment of this part's payload as JSON.

query.description: This part's question's text: a bytes attachment of a JSON string.

request_id.description: The id this part's call carries, as [`ForecastStep::request_id`].

top_k.description: How many candidates each row keeps, as [`Ranking::top_k`].

candidates.description:
The candidate each question asks after, the first question's first,
one per question: a bytes attachment of a JSON list of
[`GivenCandidate`]s, as [`Materialize::candidates`] gives them.

parts.description: Each later question, in the order of the candidates.

FrameQuestionScope.description:
The meaning of one independently gathered question for error presentation.
This selects no native action and identifies no suspended computation.

ReplyId.description: Names one fetch or model call within a run, so its reply can be matched.

oneOf.description:
The rows, as an Arrow attachment. With a `continuation`, they are
one page of the answer, and more follow: the core asks again for
the same request with that continuation, opaque to it, until a page
comes without one (design choice 1, paging), and reads the pages as
one answer; nothing is truncated silently. Every page holds the
same schema.

ProviderError.description:
A provider's failure: its kind, whether trying again may succeed, and
the driver's own SQLSTATE, vendor code and error class, and its message
as a diagnostic for the data layer alone. What the failure means is the
data layer's to say ([`DataLayer::failure`]), from these facts; the
message is never echoed into an error the core gives, since drivers
quote values there (decision H17).

error_class.description:
The driver's error class, a name of its closed list such as
Databricks's `INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS` (contract v28, T3.27), read
as the old client reads it (`error_class`: the driver's own answer,
else the bracketed name its message opens with). Left out, none.

driver_message.description:
The driver's message, passed through by the host unread (contract
v28, T3.6): an internal diagnostic only [`DataLayer::failure`] reads,
where the old client reads a failure by its text (Snowflake's
"does not exist", `SNOW/table.py:34-45`), and never echoed into a
public error (decision H17). Left out, none.

ErrorKind.description: What kind of problem an error is.

oneOf.description: The caller's request is not one the core accepts.

A valid request the core does not support, such as a type outside
the closed set.
Something the request names does not exist.
The data source or its driver failed.
The model endpoint or its transport failed.
The run was cancelled.

The host broke the run protocol: a call in the wrong state, a reply
the run did not ask for, a malformed control message.
A defect in the core, a contained panic included.

The endpoint answered, with any HTTP status; the body is an
attachment of the bytes received.

The transport failed before an answer: its kind and whether trying
again may succeed; the transport's message stays in the host.

The endpoint failed with no body to hand over, as an SDK's error
reports it (contract v28, T3.27, for T3.13): what the host was told.

ModelAnswer.description:
A model call's failure as the host's transport reported it
([`ModelOutcome::Failed`]): the HTTP status, and the facts the core
reads the endpoint's own codes from. The detail can quote the request,
so it travels as an attachment, and the core reads it only for codes,
never repeating it.

detail.description:
A bytes attachment of the error's message or the REST body, as UTF-8
text, if any.

provider_code.description:
The error code the SDK's error carries apart from its message
(`error_code`), if any.

provider_error.description: The name of the SDK error's class (`BadRequest`), if any.

FetchStep.description:
One data request of a fetch step, with how the run's provider answers
it: the SQL statements its data layer planned, or the request passed to
a host provider, and the schema the answer must have.

continuation.description:
The continuation the provider's last page of this request gave
([`FetchOutcome::Data::continuation`]), asking for the rows after
it; left out on a request's first fetch (design choice 1, paging).

purpose.description:
Why the run asks it, where a host or a comparison of the run's
statements with the old client's needs to know: `locate`, a read of
a table as it stands at this `materialize` (its namespace, catalog,
keys and preview), which the owner's plan B adds and the old client
made once, at `from_source` (contract v28, T3.4). Left out, a read
of the operation's own.

oneOf.description:
One part of the catalog for the tables named (all when empty): what
the provider returns is in the shape its plan expects, which the
data layer reads into a [`CatalogAnswer`].

Every matching row of `table`, `columns` in order, paged through to
the end; `limit` asks for any `limit` rows instead.
The first rows of `table`, for inference.

For each key, in order, one row: its label (its position, where it
gives none), the table's rows, the key's distinct values among rows
holding all of it, and the rows missing any part of it, as the
reference's single `UNION ALL` reads them.

For each time column, in order, one row: its position and the
smallest and largest `CAST(column AS TIMESTAMP)`, as the reference's
single `UNION ALL` reads them.

One row: the rows of `table`, then, for each of `columns` in order,
its smallest and largest value, each of the column's own type and
null when no row holds one, and the rows holding a value, read over
every row in one statement, as the reference's time column choice
reads a table its preview may not hold whole (`_full_range`).

At most one row: a value of `key` that more than one row of `table`
holds, among the rows holding every part of it, as the reference
reads one to show a repeated key (`_repeated_key_sql`).

A seeded sample of `n` entities of `table` by `key`: `columns` in
order, from the rows meeting every filter. `key_dtype`, where given,
is the data type of a key of one column the draw orders by: the type
the source declares it where its catalog fixes one, else the
schema's; a dialect that hashes only some types (SQLite's, which
hashes an integer key and the `rowid` otherwise) chooses by it once
for the column. Left out, the dialect decides by itself.

rows.description:
The rows `table` holds, where the provider sizes its draw by
them ([`ProviderCapabilities::sample_rows`]): the core counts
them (`count_rows`) before it samples and names the count here,
as the reference's warehouse samplers read each table's rows
first (contract v28). Left out for any other provider.

oneOf.description:
The rows of `table` whose `key` equals a seed's key, `columns` in
order after the seed's batch position (decision H15). `key` names the
table's key columns in order, one or several (design choice 1; a key
of several is groundwork, [`seed_key_columns`]);
`seeds` holds the key's columns ([`seed_key_columns`]), `batch` and
the seed time columns `window` names. With `per_seed`, at most that many rows per seed, first in
`order`, and the result is ordered by `(batch, order)`; without it,
there is no `order` and the result is unordered.

One row per seed whose key `table` holds, `columns` in order after
the seed's batch position and the count of rows holding its key;
which row of a key several rows hold is not defined. `key` and
`seeds` as `neighbors`'.

DescribePart.description: Which part of the catalog a `describe` reads.

oneOf.description:
The source's table names: one row per table. With tables named,
the relations, tables or views, the source would read under any of
those names written unqualified, by its own resolution of such a
name (on DuckDB, through its search path): none when it would read
none, which is how the core learns a name the caller gave is not
the source's, never by matching names itself (T1.23, decision
E59).

Each table's columns, with their declared types, nullability and
primary-key flags.
Each table's declared primary and unique keys.
Each table's declared foreign keys.

The tables' indexes, which feed the reference's "Missing N indices"
warning: the source's whole, or one table's where the provider's
index advice reads them so ([`IndexAdvice::LeadingColumn`]).

The columns of one index, named by a relation as a table is (an
index is its schema's object): one row per column, in the index's
order, its name, null for an expression. Asked for an index whose
columns the catalog's list of keys or indexes does not give
(SQLite's `index_info`, as the reference reads it). A host provider
is never asked it: its `keys` and `indexes` answers give each key's
and index's columns ([`catalog_columns`]), so no key or index it
lists is read by its name.

The namespace a relation of one part is read in, as the source names
a table it holds: one row per part, outermost first, its name
(contract v28, T3.8): a Postgres source's current schema, under
which the reference names a table it cannot find; no row for a
source whose tables are named alone (DuckDB's, SQLite's). Asked only
to name a table the source lacks.

The exact names of the tables in the named table's namespace whose
declared primary keys the source enforces (T3.6). Asked lazily once
per namespace, only before counting a key containing that declared
primary key, when `key_enforcement` is declared. A failed or unreadable
listing establishes no enforcement. It does not change lookup checks.

The definition of the one semantic model named (contract v28, T3.27):
a Databricks metric view's `DESCRIBE TABLE EXTENDED`, a Snowflake
semantic view's `SYSTEM$READ_YAML_FROM_SEMANTIC_VIEW`, read into
[`CatalogAnswer::ViewDefinition`]. Only a SQL provider whose dialect
reads views is asked it; every other dialect refuses it by name
([`Sentence::ViewsUnread`]), and a host provider is never asked it.

Filter.description:
A condition on the rows a request reads; a request's filters are a
conjunction.

oneOf.description: The row's `columns` equal one of the key set's rows.

KeySet.description: A set of keys: an Arrow attachment, and the columns it holds.

Bound.description: One bound of a time range.

TableKey.description: Columns of a table that together make a key.

label.description:
The number a `key_counts` row for this key is labelled with, where
not its position among the keys asked: the reference labels each by
its table's place among the tables with a key, a key it does not
count included (T2.12).

unique.description:
The source keeps the key unique (a declared primary or unique key
that may still hold a null): its distinct values are the rows
holding all of it, which a rendering may count as the rows less
those missing part of it, as the reference counts such a key
(`_key_count_sql`; contract v28, carried row P2-T2.2-3). The count
is the same either way.

Window2.description:
The rows of a `neighbors` request in time: the window column between
the bounds a seed gives. A row whose window column is NULL is not
returned when a window is set.

source_type.description:
The current catalog declaration of the window column, when known.
Only the dialect interprets it: zoned timestamp instants compare
with UTC seed bounds; NTZ and DATE retain their wall clock. Absent
for older callers, preserving their existing rendering.

SeedBound.description:
One bound of a `neighbors` window: a seed time column, compared with the
window column in the source's own `CAST(column AS TIMESTAMP)` wall clock.

seed_column.description: A zone-less `timestamp[ns]` column of the seed key set.

NeighborLimit.description:
The caller's per-seed neighbor bound, interpreted by its provider.
Positive counts retain their original unsigned JSON representation.
SQL expressions are caller-authored query code under the same trust
boundary as derived relation expressions, never identifiers or values.

anyOf.description: A negative JSON number's exact text, including fractional bounds.

TieBreak.description:
The total order a `neighbors` request keeps per seed, built by the core
from the reference's rule (design, "Data access").

as_timestamp.description:
Order by `CAST(column AS TIMESTAMP)`, the source's wall clock,
rather than the column's own values.

nulls_last.description:
Nulls after every value; the core writes the order the provider
declares (`ProviderCapabilities::null_order`).

FetchPlan.description:
How a provider answers one request (decision H14): SQL statements run
in order on one session, the last one's rows the answer, or the typed
request itself, passed to a host provider that answers it; either way
with the Arrow schema the whole plan returns, and answered with one
attachment holding every row.

SqlStatement.description: One statement a SQL provider runs.

SqlParam.description:
A statement's parameter: a scalar, or a key set the statement's text
reads under `relation`. How the keys come to be read by that name is
the dialect's, which `sdm-data` renders and its provider binds: the
DuckDB provider registers the attachment as a relation of that name; a
PostgreSQL dialect may bind the keys as JSON text that a common table
expression of that name unpacks, as the reference's PostgreSQL sampler
does. `relation` names what the text reads, not an instruction to
register an Arrow relation. A dialect that binds its key sets as JSON
text names none: [`DataLayer::bind`] turns each into a `text` parameter.

A `text` parameter (contract v28, T3.27) binds the one text cell of a
one-row, one-column Arrow attachment: a key set the dialect writes as
JSON text itself, past the control message's size ([`DataLayer::bind`]).
In a [`BoundFetch`] the attachment is a local reference the data layer
chose; the core installs its batch in the run and names it here by the
run's own id before the step is sent.

ExpectedSchema.description:
The Arrow schema a request expects back, or that the answer discovers
it (a preview, a scan).

SqlResultConversion.description:
A native result conversion selected by the SQL data layer.
Column positions are zero-based and names remain exactly the
warehouse's original output names, including duplicates.

oneOf.description:
PostgreSQL zoned values read as text, including array elements and
range bounds, use canonical UTC without changing the session.
This policy applies to the whole result, not one projection.

SqlTimestampKind.description:
The timestamp meaning used by the core's SQL projection, retained
through key-set binding and chunk re-rendering. A host transfers the
projected integer unchanged for either kind.

oneOf.description: A timestamp's physical instant, measured from the Unix epoch.

A timezone-free timestamp's civil fields, measured from the
epoch's wall fields without assigning any local timezone.

FetchPurpose.description: Why a run asks a fetch ([`FetchStep::purpose`]).

oneOf.description: A read of a table as it stands at this `materialize`.

Endpoint.description: Which model endpoint a call goes to.

OperationResult.description: One operation's result, the payload of the run's last step.

oneOf.description: A query's validation: accepted, or refused with PQL's diagnostics.

query.description:
What the core resolved of an accepted query (contract v28, T3.8),
which a host reads instead of resolving the query again: its facts
and its text as the core writes it back. Absent for a refused query
and from a core that does not say.

oneOf.description: `describe_source`'s result.

description.description: A bytes attachment of a [`SourceDescription`] as JSON.

frame_rows.description:
Table-stage frames only: the detached Arrow table, taken before
dropping this Run and rebound with fresh ids for Schema. Never
present in SQL/Schema results or persistent schema metadata.

frame_decimals.description:
Table-stage rows only: JSON NativeDecimalColumn declarations needed
when rebinding owned scale-zero mantissas under fresh attachment ids.

notes.description:
What a semantic model's conversion notes of the schema it gave
(contract v28, T3.27): each measure as the predictive query it is,
each time column taken in place of the view's own, each parameter
read as its default, in order (`Schema.conversion_notes`). Given at
describe only. Left out, none.

oneOf.description: `edit_schema`'s result.

schema.description:
A bytes attachment of a [`HeldSchema`] as JSON: the schema with the
edit made, which the host holds from now on: each column's data
type, meanings and source facts, each table's key, time column and
repeated keys, and the links.

declared.description:
The column the edit gave a meaning the caller chose (the reference's
`Column.stype_declared`): the column whose meaning was assigned, or
the time column named, which is assigned `timestamp`; none for any
other edit.

oneOf.description: A materialized request, held by the host and handed back to `predict`.

query.description:
What the core resolved of the query it gathered (contract v26,
T2.18), which a host reads instead of resolving the query itself:
the core resolves a query naming any column (KO2-36), which a host's
own validator may not. Absent from a core that does not say.

oneOf.description:
The prediction. Nothing inline grows with the result's width or the
endpoint's answer (decision H5).

result.description:
An Arrow attachment, one row per answer, ordered by `row_index` as
the reference's result frame orders them (T1.28b), whose schema
names its columns in order: `row_index`, `id`, `id_as_written` where
the ids are not all integers or all text (utf8: the JSON text of the
reference's item value, null where there was none), `forecast_step`
where an answer given as written carries one, `prediction` where an
answer carries one, `prediction_as_answered` where the prediction
column changed an answer (utf8: the JSON text of the reference's item
value, null where there was none; present only for a regression's
integer widened among doubles or a class written as a non-finite
number), `probabilities` where an answer carries them, and
`answer_index`, each answer's place in the endpoint's order
(`sdm_request::predict::table`).

Contract v26 fixes the columns ranking and forecasting add (design
choice 1; written from T2.8 and T2.9), after `probabilities` and
before `answer_index`, each where an answer carries it: `scores`
(list of float64, an item's scores in the endpoint's order),
`rankings` (list of utf8, an item's rankings, each a mapping), and
`quantiles` (a regression's quantiles, each named as the endpoint
named it, in the order written; from contract v27, T2.9, a
mapping-valued field, laid out as the next paragraph says, an
answer's `{}` the text `{}`, none null).

A mapping-valued field (T2.8, contract v27) is laid out as JSON
object text in a Utf8 column, and a list of mappings as a list of
those texts: a JSON object when every key is text, otherwise (a key
that is a number, a boolean or null) the JSON list of its `[key,
value]` pairs, as a JSON object holds no other key. Each is read
from the answer as Python's `dict` reads it, keys equal as Python's
are, by the one reader `sdm_wire::response::mapping`.

A ranking's result (T2.8, contract v27), one row per entity asked
about, in place
of `prediction` and `probabilities`: `rankings` (the candidates the
row ranks, best first, at most `top_k`, each the JSON text of its
value, as the state names it), `scores` (how sure the endpoint was
of each, in the same order) and `candidates` (list of int64, each
one's position among the candidates `materialize` was given, its
first where it was given more than once, in the same order), which a
host gives back as the outputs named in `outputs`, each candidate as
the value it was given as, found by its position.

Contract v27 adds, after those, `embeddings` (list of float64, an
answer's embedding in the order written, null where it has none;
T2.11).

model.description: The model that answered, as the endpoint names it.

request_id.description:
The endpoint's id for the call; empty for a request with no row to
score, answered without a call.

metadata.description: A bytes attachment of the endpoint's `metadata` object as JSON.

outputs.description:
The outputs the call asked for, the task's default ones where the
caller named none.

unscored_candidates.description:
A ranking's candidates no question was sent for, the context sampled
for each holding one answer only (T2.8): each its position among the
candidates `materialize` was given (of a request held, among the
candidates it holds, T3.26), in the order named. Empty for any other
result.

value.description: The complete useful PreparedFrameValue as input-sized JSON.

oneOf.description: Owned model response data. The attachments are data, never resume handles.

PqlDiagnostic.description: One PQL diagnostic: its code and where in the query text it points.

ViewNote.description:
A note of a semantic model's conversion ([`DescribedSource::notes`]):
its sentence, a note's ([`crate::Code::Note`]), the fields its template
names, and what it is about, so a host shows it only while the schema
still holds that: the table it names, and the time column it says was
taken, as the old client drops a note of a table not taken or of a
time column the table no longer has (`CL/schema.py:1401-1433`).

table.description:
The schema's table the note is about; none for a note of the whole
view (a parameter's).

time_column.description: The time column the note says was taken, of `table`.

sentence.description:
What the error says, of [`ErrorCode`]'s sentences: the template each
host fills, read only for wording (T3.17).

part.description:
Where the error happened in a question asked in parts (a forecast's
step, a ranking's candidate), a sentence of [`Code::Part`] said after
the error's own; none for any other error (T3.17 fix 2).

message.description: For a person to read; not promised, and never holding an input value.

fields.description: What callers branch on, by name.

public_details.description:
When native compatibility requires its exact public details, keep
presentation-only fields separate from what callers branch on.
Absence preserves the existing shared error details convention.

cause.description: The error this one was raised from.

retryable.description:
Whether the same call may succeed if tried again; carried from
provider and transport errors, false otherwise.

drop_held.description:
The states the host handed this run that it must drop rather than
hand back again: the core refused them, so a later run given them
would be refused the same way (decision E74). The host follows this
alone, never reading which field an error names; empty for any
other error.

answered.description:
What a request asked in several model calls had been answered when
a later call failed (design choice 1, `main`'s answered parts,
T2.8c): the error keeps what was paid for, so the rest can be asked
again. Absent for any other error.

ErrorCode.description:
The codes the core gives: one closed list, so each host's mapping
matches every code with no catch-all arm (decision H6). Host and core
ship together, so the list is exhaustive; a new code is a contract
version bump. PQL's own diagnostic codes stay strings inside
`PqlDiagnostic`.

oneOf.description: The caller's request is not one the core accepts.
A valid request this core does not support.
The model endpoint answered with something the core cannot read.
The host's configuration of a run is not one the core accepts.

The transport to the model endpoint failed: it could not reach the
endpoint, or could not read its answer.
A defect in the core, a contained panic included.
The model a request names does not exist.
An optional dependency of the host is not installed.
A schema the core cannot work with.
The endpoint does not support sessions.
An Arrow type outside the closed set.
A value the admitted type of its column cannot hold, such as a `timestamp[s]` past the microseconds an int64 counts.
A provider answered with a schema other than the one asked for.
A provider's query failed.
A reply for an id the run is not waiting on: unknown, stale or already answered.
`next` was called before every reply the run asked for arrived.
A reply of the wrong kind: a model answer for a fetch, or the other way round.
The run was used after it finished.
The run was used after it was cancelled.
The run was used after a panic poisoned it.
A second call reached a run while one was in progress.
A control message the contract cannot read, larger than the control cap, of the wrong direction, or whose attachments do not match the ids it names.

A model serving endpoint refused the request, with an HTTP status and
perhaps a code of its own (contract v28, T3.27): the host raises its
endpoint-refusal error with the status ([`REFUSED_STATUS`]) and the
code ([`REFUSED_CODE`], none where there is none), as the old client
raises `NimRequestError(status, code=...)`, the error's other fields
its details.

HeldState.description:
A state a host holds between runs and hands back to the core with a
later run's start, opaque to it.

oneOf.description:
The sampler state a materializer's last run left
(`Materialize.sampler_state`, decision E52).

AnsweredParts.description: The answers a failed request had received ([`CoreError::answered`]).

result.description:
An Arrow attachment of the answers received, laid out as
`Predicted.result`, travelling with the error.
